titleEn: Until the Snow Stops, Let Us Play!

pages.text: "Snow, stop!" Pipo pressed his nose to the kitchen window and shouted. Snow fell thickly, covering yard and wall. His feet longed to run in the snow with the sheep.
"Mom, I want to run with the sheep!" He ran toward the door. Adding firewood, Mom shook her head. "When the snow stops. The sheep are in their pen now too."
Pipo returned to the window and stamped. "Still snowing? When will it stop?" Flakes stuck to the glass and melted. "Bored—!" He tapped the window with his palms.
On a stool by the stove, Grandpa Sheep tapped his stick. "Pipo, until the snow stops, let us play! This was our game on snowy days long ago." He sat a step back from the stove and held up both hands.
A big shadow appeared on the wall. Ears pricked—a sheep! "A sheep! Baa—!" Pipo laughed. Grandpa wiggled his fingers, and the shadow sheep nodded.
"Now Pipo's turn." Pipo sat beside him and held up both hands. A shadow with floppy ears appeared. "A puppy! Me, me!" He pretended to bark.
Sheep and puppy shadows walked side by side on the wall. "Until the snow stops, let us play!" Pipo sang happily along. Mom smiled by the stove.
Pipo crouched with hands at his chest, not bored at all. But the window was bright; no more flakes stuck. Turning his head from that very pose, he called, "Grandpa, Mom! The snow stopped!"
Pipo flung the door open and ran outside. "One, stop watching the window! Two, sit back from the stove! Three, take turns with Grandpa!" He had played plenty of shadows while waiting.
Pipo bounced with the sheep in the snow. He hugged Grandpa's waist when Grandpa followed him out. "Let us play again!" In Grandpa's arms, he called, "Until the snow stops, let us play!"
